title: UNIT 5: HUMAN BODY SYSTEM
notes: ✓ Human body systems work together for coordination, control and maintenance of a stable internal environment.

title: 5.1 THE NERVOUS SYSTEM
notes:
✓ Nervous system → highly complex coordination system that provides rapid responses to internal and external changes.

✓ Main divisions → Central nervous system (CNS) + Peripheral nervous system (PNS).

◆ CNS → brain + spinal cord.
◆ PNS → nerves outside the CNS.

title: 5.1.1 FUNCTIONS OF THE NERVOUS SYSTEM
notes:
✓ Detects changes/stimuli.
✓ Carries sensory information to the CNS.
✓ Processes and interprets information.
✓ Sends instructions to effectors.
✓ Coordinates body activities and responses.

title: 5.2 TYPES OF THE NERVOUS SYSTEM
notes:
✓ Central nervous system (CNS) → brain + spinal cord.

✓ Peripheral nervous system (PNS) → nerves connecting the CNS with organs, limbs and skin.

title: 5.2.1 THE BRAIN
notes:
✓ Brain → major control center protected by the skull and meninges.

◆ Cerebrum → largest part; reasoning, speech, memory, learning, emotions, sensory interpretation and voluntary movement.

◆ Cerebellum → coordination of movement, posture and balance.

◆ Brainstem → connects brain with spinal cord and controls many automatic functions such as breathing, heartbeat, swallowing and coughing.

title: BRAIN REGIONS & FUNCTIONS
notes:
✓ Hypothalamus → homeostatic control; regulates thirst, appetite and body temperature; links nervous and endocrine systems.

✓ Thalamus → involved mainly in sensation and relay of information.

✓ Midbrain → relay pathways and visual/auditory/tactile reflexes.

✓ Pons → relay center; assists regulation of breathing.

✓ Medulla oblongata → regulates heartbeat, breathing, blood pressure, vomiting, coughing, sneezing and swallowing.

title: PROTECTION OF THE CNS
notes:
✓ Skull → protects brain.

✓ Vertebral column → protects spinal cord.

✓ Meninges → dura mater + arachnoid mater + pia mater.

✓ Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) → cushions the CNS, helps maintain pressure and permits limited exchange of nutrients/wastes.

title: GREY & WHITE MATTER
notes:
✓ Grey matter → mainly neuron cell bodies.

✓ White matter → mainly bundles of axons.

✓ Spinal cord → grey matter mainly inside, white matter outside.

title: 5.2.2 THE SPINAL CORD
notes:
✓ Spinal cord → tubular nervous tissue extending from the brainstem and protected by vertebrae.

✓ Spinal nerves → connect the spinal cord with the rest of the body.

◆ Afferent nerves → carry information toward the CNS.
◆ Efferent nerves → carry instructions away from the CNS.

title: 5.3 THE PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM
notes:
✓ PNS → all nerves outside the brain and spinal cord.

✓ Main role → connects the CNS with organs, limbs and skin and carries information to and from the CNS.

✓ Divisions → Somatic nervous system + Autonomic nervous system.

title: 5.3.1 SOMATIC NERVOUS SYSTEM
notes:
✓ Somatic nervous system → carries sensory and motor information to and from the CNS.

✓ Responsible mainly for sensory information and voluntary movement.

title: 5.3.2 AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM
notes:
✓ Autonomic nervous system → controls involuntary functions such as heartbeat, blood flow, digestion and breathing.

◆ Sympathetic → fight-or-flight → ↑ heart rate, ↑ breathing, ↑ blood flow to muscles, sweating, pupil dilation.

◆ Parasympathetic → rest-and-conserve → ↓ heart rate, ↓ breathing, ↓ muscle blood flow, pupil constriction.

title: 5.3.3 NEURONS & THEIR FUNCTIONS
notes:
✓ Neuron → basic communication cell of the nervous system.

✓ Main parts:

◆ Cell body (soma) → contains nucleus; maintains structure and provides energy.

◆ Dendrites → receive signals.

◆ Axon → carries nerve impulses away from the cell body.

◆ Myelin sheath → insulates axon and increases impulse speed.

◆ Node of Ranvier → gaps in myelin that facilitate rapid impulse conduction.

title: 5.3.4 TYPES OF NEURONS
notes:
✓ Sensory/afferent neuron → receptor → CNS.

✓ Motor/efferent neuron → CNS → effector.

✓ Interneuron/relay neuron → connects neurons within the CNS.

✓ Motor neurons → upper motor neurons + lower motor neurons.

title: NERVOUS RESPONSE PATHWAY
notes: ✓ Stimulus → sensory receptor → afferent neuron → CNS/interneuron → efferent neuron → effector → response.

title: SYNAPSES
notes:
✓ Synapse → gap between communicating neurons.

✓ Impulse reaches axon terminal → neurotransmitters released → cross synaptic gap → bind to receptors on next cell → new electrical impulse begins.

✓ Neurotransmitter → chemical messenger between neurons or between neurons and muscles.

title: 5.3.5 NERVE IMPULSE & TRANSMISSION
notes:
✓ Nerve impulse → electrical event caused by changes in charge across the axon membrane.

✓ Resting potential ≈ −70 mV.

✓ Threshold potential ≈ −55 mV.

◆ Depolarization → Na⁺ enters the neuron and membrane becomes less negative.

◆ Action potential → rapid reversal of membrane potential after threshold is reached.

◆ Hyperpolarization → membrane becomes more negative than normal.

◆ Refractory period → short period when the neuron is difficult to re-excite.

title: NEUROTRANSMITTERS
notes:
✓ Neurotransmitters → chemical messengers used to transmit signals across synapses.

◆ Acetylcholine (ACh) → abundant neurotransmitter found in both CNS and PNS.
◆ Excitatory transmitter → promotes action-potential generation.
◆ Inhibitory transmitter → decreases likelihood of action-potential generation.
◆ Neuromodulator → regulates activity of groups of neurons over a slower time scale.

title: 5.1.3 REFLEXES
notes:
✓ Reflex action → sudden, automatic and uncontrolled response to a stimulus.

✓ Examples → withdrawal from heat • blinking • pupillary light reflex • breathing.

✓ Reflexes protect the body and can occur without conscious processing before the response.

title: REFLEX ARC
notes:
✓ Reflex arc → neural pathway involved in a reflex.

✓ Receptor → afferent neuron → relay/interneuron in CNS → efferent neuron → effector → response.

◆ Dorsal root → sensory/afferent entry.
◆ Ventral root → motor/efferent exit.

title: 5.4 DRUG ABUSE
notes:
✓ Drug → substance that can change mental or physical state.

✓ Drug use → use of a substance that affects brain/body function or mental activity.
✓ Drug abuse → excessive use and/or dependence.
✓ Drug dependence → repeated use leading to addiction.
✓ Withdrawal symptoms → unpleasant effects after suddenly stopping a drug.

title: 5.4.1 COMMON DRUGS USED IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
✓ Commonly abused substances → alcohol • khat • tobacco • cannabis • solvents.

✓ Other drugs discussed → heroin • cocaine • LSD • ecstasy.

✓ Drug abuse can affect the nervous system, behavior, health and social life.

title: 5.4.2 SMOKING
notes:
✓ Nicotine → addictive drug in cigarette smoke; affects the brain and can produce temporary feelings of calm/well-being.
✓ Cigarette smoke contains many harmful chemicals.
✓ Long-term smoking is associated with serious health problems.

title: 5.4.3 ALCOHOL
notes:
✓ Alcohol → psychoactive, addictive and poisonous substance.

✓ Small amounts → relaxation and reduced inhibition.
✓ Excess/chronic use → serious health problems and dependence.
✓ Alcohol strongly affects the brain and other body systems.

title: 5.4.4 KHAT
notes:
✓ Khat (Catha edulis) → plant whose young leaves/buds are chewed for stimulant effects.

✓ Active drug → cathinone.
✓ Effects → stimulation, euphoria, reduced appetite.
✓ Dependence/withdrawal → depression, tiredness and difficulty concentrating.

title: CANNABIS
notes:
✓ Cannabis → plant containing cannabinoids; THC is its major psychoactive compound.

✓ THC affects brain areas involved in memory, emotion and motivation.
✓ Can produce relaxation, euphoria and altered perception.
✓ Hallucinogenic effects may cause distorted sensations or perceptions.

title: 5.5 SENSE ORGANS
notes:
✓ Sense organs → detect stimuli and relay information to the brain.

✓ Major sense organs covered → skin • tongue • nose • eye • ear.

title: 5.5.1 SKIN
notes:
✓ Skin functions → touch • temperature • pressure • pain • protection • water conservation • excretion through sweat • temperature regulation.

✓ Three main layers:

◆ Epidermis → outer protective layer; limits water loss and pathogen entry.

◆ Dermis → blood vessels, sensory receptors, hair follicles and sweat glands.

◆ Hypodermis → fatty/connective tissue; energy storage and insulation.

title: 5.5.2 TONGUE
notes:
✓ Tongue → muscular organ important in chewing, swallowing, speech and taste.

✓ Papillae → small projections containing taste buds.
✓ Five basic tastes → sweet • sour • salty • bitter • umami.
✓ Taste receptors are distributed across the tongue rather than being restricted to separate taste zones.

title: 5.5.3 NOSE
notes:
✓ Nose → organ of smell and part of the respiratory pathway.

✓ Olfactory receptors → detect odor molecules.
✓ Olfactory bulb → involved in processing smell information.
✓ Olfactory nerve → carries signals to the brain.
✓ Nose also warms, humidifies and filters inhaled air.

title: 5.5.4 EYE: STRUCTURE
notes:
✓ Sclera → tough protective outer layer.
✓ Cornea → transparent front surface; refracts incoming light.
✓ Iris → controls pupil diameter.
✓ Pupil → opening through which light enters.
✓ Lens → focuses light onto retina.
✓ Choroid → vascular layer that nourishes the eye and reduces internal reflection.
✓ Retina → light-sensitive layer containing rods and cones.
✓ Optic nerve → carries visual impulses to the brain.

title: EYE: VISION & LIGHT CONTROL
notes:
✓ Dim light → radial muscles contract + circular muscles relax → pupil dilates.

✓ Bright light → circular muscles contract + radial muscles relax → pupil constricts.

✓ Vision pathway → light → cornea → pupil → lens → retina → optic nerve → brain.

title: EYE PHOTORECEPTORS
notes:
✓ Rods → highly sensitive to light; important for dim-light and black-and-white vision.

✓ Cones → function mainly in bright light and detect color.

✓ Fovea centralis → high concentration of cones; highest visual resolution and color vision.

✓ Blind spot/optic disc → point where optic nerve leaves the eye; no retina is present.

title: COMMON EYE DEFECTS
notes:
✓ Myopia (short-sight) → distant objects difficult to see clearly.

✓ Hypermetropia/hyperopia (long-sight) → near objects difficult to see clearly.

✓ Cataract → clouding of the lens.

✓ Glaucoma → associated with increased pressure and damage to the eye.

✓ Color blindness → difficulty distinguishing certain colors.

✓ Corrections depend on the defect and may include suitable lenses or medical treatment.

title: 5.5.5 EAR: STRUCTURE
notes:
✓ Three regions → Outer ear • Middle ear • Inner ear.

✓ Outer ear → pinna + ear canal + eardrum.
✓ Middle ear → malleus + incus + stapes; connected to throat by Eustachian tube.
✓ Inner ear → cochlea + utriculus + sacculus + semicircular canals.

title: MECHANISM OF HEARING
notes: ✓ Sound waves → pinna → ear canal → eardrum vibrates → ossicles amplify/transmit vibrations → oval window → cochlear fluid moves → sensory hair cells stimulated → nerve impulses → auditory nerve → brain.

title: BALANCE & MOVEMENT
notes:
✓ Semicircular canals → detect rotational/head movement.

✓ Ampullae contain sensory cells and hairs within the cupula.

✓ Head movement → fluid movement → cupula bends → sensory cells stimulated → nerve impulses → brain interprets movement.

✓ The three semicircular canals lie in different planes and detect movement in different directions.

title: 5.6 ENDOCRINE SYSTEM
notes:
✓ Endocrine system → coordinates body functions through hormones.

✓ Hormones → chemical messengers released into body fluids, mainly blood.

✓ Endocrine glands → ductless; release hormones directly into blood.

✓ Target organ → tissue containing receptors for a particular hormone.

✓ Endocrine responses are generally slower but longer-lasting than nervous responses.

title: ENDOCRINE vs EXOCRINE GLANDS
notes:
✓ Endocrine → no ducts → hormones released into blood.

✓ Exocrine → ducts → secretions delivered to a surface or cavity.

◆ Examples of exocrine glands → sweat • salivary • sebaceous • lacrimal • mammary.
✓ Pancreas → both endocrine and exocrine.

title: PROTEIN vs STEROID HORMONES
notes:
✓ Protein hormones → bind receptors on cell membranes → activate intracellular/secondary-messenger pathways such as cAMP.

✓ Steroid hormones → lipid-soluble → enter target cells → bind intracellular receptors → affect gene expression → new proteins are produced.

title: 5.6.2 HYPOTHALAMUS
notes:
✓ Hypothalamus → connects nervous and endocrine systems.

✓ Produces releasing/inhibiting signals controlling the pituitary.
✓ Produces hormones stored/released through the posterior pituitary.
✓ Regulates major internal functions and contributes to homeostasis.

title: 5.6.3 PITUITARY GLAND
notes:
✓ Pituitary gland → small gland in the brain; coordinates many endocrine functions.

✓ Anterior pituitary → hormonally controlled by hypothalamus.

✓ Posterior pituitary → under nervous control; stores/releases hormones produced by hypothalamus.

◆ Anterior pituitary hormones → GH • ACTH • TSH • FSH • LH • PRL.
◆ Posterior pituitary → ADH + oxytocin.

title: 5.6.4 THYROID GLAND
notes:
✓ Thyroid → butterfly-shaped gland below the larynx.

◆ T3 + T4 → promote normal metabolism.
◆ Calcitonin → lowers blood calcium and phosphate levels.
◆ Hyposecretion → hypothyroidism, including goiter, cretinism and myxedema.
◆ Hypersecretion → hyperthyroidism/Graves' disease.

title: 5.6.5 PARATHYROID GLANDS
notes:
✓ Parathyroid glands → four small glands on the posterior surface of the thyroid.

✓ Hormone → parathyroid hormone (PTH).
✓ Main role → increases/regulates blood calcium level.
✓ Hyposecretion → tetany.
✓ Hypersecretion → osteitis fibrosa cystica.

title: 5.6.6 ADRENAL GLAND
notes:
✓ Adrenal glands → located above the kidneys.

✓ Cortex → outer region; three zones → zona glomerulosa • zona fasciculata • zona reticularis.

✓ Medulla → inner region; produces epinephrine/adrenaline + norepinephrine/noradrenaline.

✓ Adrenaline → fight-or-flight response → prepares the body for rapid action.

title: 5.6.7 PANCREAS
notes:
✓ Pancreas → both endocrine and exocrine gland.

✓ Islets of Langerhans → endocrine function.
◆ α-cells → glucagon → raises blood glucose.
◆ β-cells → insulin → lowers blood glucose.
◆ δ-cells → somatostatin/GHIH → helps regulate carbohydrate metabolism.
✓ Exocrine pancreas → acinar cells release digestive enzymes through ducts.

title: 5.6.8 GONADS
notes:
✓ Gonads → testes + ovaries; produce sex hormones.

◆ Ovaries → estrogen and other reproductive hormones; regulate female sexual development and reproductive functions.
◆ Testes → testosterone; promotes male secondary sexual characteristics.
✓ FSH and other pituitary hormones coordinate gonadal activity.

title: 5.6.9 PINEAL GLAND
notes:
✓ Pineal gland → pine-cone-shaped gland deep in the cerebrum.

✓ Hormone → melatonin.
✓ Function → regulates circadian rhythms, including sleep/wake cycles.

title: THYMUS GLAND
notes:
✓ Thymus → gland located between the lungs that becomes smaller over time.

✓ Produces hormones such as thymosin.
✓ Role → supports production and maturation of lymphocytes involved in body defense.

title: 5.7 EXOCRINE GLANDS
notes:
✓ Exocrine glands → release substances through ducts.

✓ Examples → salivary • sweat • sebaceous • lacrimal • ceruminous • mucous • mammary • prostate glands.

✓ Liver and pancreas have both endocrine and exocrine functions.

title: 5.8 HOMEOSTASIS
notes:
✓ Homeostasis → maintenance of a relatively stable internal environment.

✓ Major examples → regulation of body temperature • blood glucose • water balance • ion balance • chemical conditions.

✓ Nervous + endocrine systems coordinate many homeostatic responses.

title: 5.8.1 HUMAN KIDNEY
notes:
✓ Kidney → filters blood, removes wastes, produces urine and regulates water/mineral balance.

✓ Main regions → cortex • medulla • renal pelvis.
✓ Nephron → functional unit of the kidney.

title: NEPHRON & URINE FORMATION
notes:
✓ Bowman’s capsule → ultrafiltration of blood.

✓ Glomerulus → capillary network where filtration pressure develops.

✓ First coiled tubule → major reabsorption of glucose, ions and water.

✓ Loop of Henle → concentrates urine and conserves water.

✓ Second coiled tubule → major water balancing and secretion.

✓ Collecting duct → collects urine; additional water reabsorption can occur.

title: ADH & WATER BALANCE
notes:
✓ Low blood water → osmoreceptors detect increased salt concentration → pituitary releases more ADH → kidney tubules become more permeable to water → more water reabsorbed → concentrated urine.

✓ High blood water → less ADH → less water reabsorbed → large volume of dilute urine.

✓ This is negative feedback.

title: THERMOREGULATION
notes:
✓ Thermoregulation → control of internal body temperature.

✓ Core body temperature is maintained around 37°C because enzyme activity depends on suitable temperature.

✓ The body regulates heat gain/loss through physiological and behavioral mechanisms coordinated mainly by the nervous system and hypothalamus.

title: 5.8.3 OSMOREGULATION
notes:
✓ Osmoregulation → regulation of water and dissolved-ion balance in body fluids.

◆ Water gained → food + drinking.
◆ Water lost → breathing + evaporation + sweating + urine.
✓ Kidneys → remove excess water/ions or conserve them when needed.

✓ Correct water/salt balance prevents harmful osmotic changes in cells.

title: 5.8.4 CHEMICAL REGULATION
notes:
✓ Liver → regulates glucose, fats and cholesterol; breaks down excess amino acids; forms urea; breaks down worn-out red blood cells; produces bile; detoxifies many substances.

✓ Respiratory chemoreceptors → monitor chemical conditions related to O₂, CO₂ and H⁺.

◆ Central chemoreceptors → located near the medulla; detect changes in CSF pH.

◆ Peripheral chemoreceptors → aortic and carotid bodies detect changes in blood gases and related chemical conditions.

title: NEGATIVE FEEDBACK
notes:
✓ Negative feedback → response reduces the original change and helps restore normal conditions.

✓ Examples → ADH and water balance • thyroid hormone regulation • blood glucose regulation • body temperature regulation.

✓ Basic pattern → Change → receptor/sensor → control center → effector → corrective response.

title: 5.9 DRUG EFFECTS ON NERVOUS & ENDOCRINE SYSTEMS
notes:
✓ Drug abuse can interfere with normal nervous and endocrine functions.

◆ Smoking → nicotine alters brain activity and causes dependence.
◆ Alcohol → affects brain function and can cause dependence and organ damage.
◆ Khat → stimulant effects and dependence can alter mood, concentration and normal behavior.
◆ Cannabis → affects brain functions including memory, emotion and motivation.

✓ Continued abuse → biochemical and behavioral changes that can impair normal body regulation.
